extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) preparing or updating US patent filings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidelines for specifying, changing, and correcting correspondence addresses and for preparing and filing an Application Data Sheet (ADS) in U.S. patent applications (including what must be included, how inconsistencies are resolved, and permitted submission methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to specify a correspondence address at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing an application, a correspondence address must be set forth in either an application data sheet (ADS) or elsewhere in a clearly identifiable manner in any paper submitted with the application filing (37 CFR 1.33(a)). If no correspondence address is specified, the Office may treat the mailing address of the first-named inventor as the correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will direct notices and communications to the person associated with the correspondence address. For correspondence submitted via electronic filing, an electronic acknowledgment will be sent to the submitter. A daytime telephone number is requested and may be changed by any party who may change the correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority order for conflicting correspondence addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one correspondence address is specified in a single document or multiple documents provide non-matching correspondence addresses, the Office will select one address to use and will accord priority in the following order: (A) application data sheet (ADS); (B) application transmittal; (C) oath or declaration (unless power of attorney is more current); and (D) power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an ADS includes a typed correspondence address and the declaration gives a different address (e.g., address associated with a Customer Number), the Office will use the typed address on the ADS because the ADS is often the most recently created document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may change the correspondence address prior to filing an executed oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the filing of an executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 by any inventor, the correspondence address may be changed by the party who filed the application; if a patent practitioner filed the application, any other patent practitioner named in the transmittal papers may also change the correspondence address. Inventors and a person authorized to act for an assignee who filed the application may also change it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent practitioner named only on a letterhead is not considered 'named in the transmittal papers' for purposes of changing the correspondence address — a clear identification of the individual as a representative is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may change the correspondence address after an executed oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 has been filed, the correspondence address may be changed only by (A) a patent practitioner of record, (B) an assignee as provided under 37 CFR 3.71(b), or (C) all of the applicants under 37 CFR 1.41(b), unless there is an assignee of the entire interest who has acted in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a correspondence address has been established as described, subsequent changes are governed by the specific regulatory provisions above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing correspondence address in continuations/divisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Special care must be taken in continuation or divisional applications to ensure any change of correspondence address in a prior application is reflected in the continuation or divisional application; otherwise the Office may not recognize the change and mailings may go to the old address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a copy of an oath or declaration from the prior application (which designates an old correspondence address) is submitted, applicant must identify the change of correspondence address in the continuation/divisional to ensure communications are mailed to the current correspondence address. Submission of an ADS or separate paper identifying the new correspondence address is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner change of correspondence after patent issues (37 CFR 1.33(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner acting in a representative capacity whose correspondence address is the correspondence address of record in an application may change the correspondence address after the patent has issued, provided the change is accompanied by a statement that notice has been given to the patentee or owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision applies to practitioners acting in a representative capacity but does not authorize practitioners acting under 37 CFR 1.34 to change the correspondence address in an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS must comply with 37 CFR 1.76 and be titled 'Application Data Sheet'
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet (ADS) is a sheet or set of sheets containing bibliographic data arranged in the format specified by the Office and must comply with 37 CFR 1.76. An ADS must be titled 'Application Data Sheet.' When provided, the ADS becomes part of the application and must comply with 37 CFR 1.52.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ADS must be submitted when required by 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78 to claim priority/benefit to a prior application; ADS use is preferred by the Office to facilitate electronic data capture but is not always mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS required section headings and bibliographic data
rubrics_metrics.description: An ADS must contain all the section headings listed in 37 CFR 1.76(b) (unless excepted) with appropriate data for each: (1) inventor information; (2) correspondence information; (3) application information; (4) representative information; (5) domestic benefit information; (6) foreign priority information; and (7) applicant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each heading carries specific required content: inventor (legal name, residence, mailing address), correspondence (address or customer number), application (title, total drawing sheets, suggested drawing figure for publication, docket number, application type, secrecy order disclosure), representative (registration numbers of practitioners), domestic benefit (continuity data), foreign priority (foreign application number/country/filing date), applicant (name/address of applicant entity or person). Empty headings are interpreted to mean no corresponding data in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS governs inconsistencies with other documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For inconsistencies between information supplied in an ADS and other documents, the most recent submission generally governs; the most recent ADS governs foreign priority (37 CFR 1.55) and domestic benefit (37 CFR 1.78) claims, while inventorship and changes to inventorship are governed by 37 CFR 1.41 and 1.48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The information in the ADS will govern when inconsistent with information supplied at the same time by a designation of correspondence address or an inventor's oath or declaration, and will govern over certain international forms (PCT Request Forms, Patent Law Treaty Model Forms) when inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and format for correcting or updating an ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in a previously submitted ADS or other information of record may be corrected or updated until payment of the issue fee by filing a new ADS providing corrected or updated information. Any ADS filed after the filing date or after a first ADS is considered a corrected/updated ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A corrected ADS must identify changes with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for deletions (except identification is not required for an ADS included with an initial 35 U.S.C. 371 submission). Identification of changes should be made relative to the most recent filing receipt. Use of the corrected Web-based ADS is recommended where permitted because it pre-populates with information of record and creates PDF version with proper strike-through and underlining. Corrected Web-based ADS is not permitted in international/national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, provisional, plant, reexamination, and supplemental examination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet must be signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unsigned application data sheet will be treated only as a transmittal letter (i.e., not as the ADS of record).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted submission methods and fillable forms for ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office provides fillable forms (PTO/AIA/14 for post-September 16, 2012 applications and PTO/SB/14 for earlier ones) and an enhanced Web-based ADS for submission. The Office's fillable form is designed to be completed electronically and filed via Patent Center or in paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data will only load directly into the USPTO electronic system when PTO/AIA/14 or PTO/SB/14 is submitted as a Fillable Form rather than a scanned PDF image. Web-based ADS and corrected Web-based ADS are available to registered filers; a corrected Web-based ADS is pre-populated with information of record and will create the appropriate PDF with strike-through/underlining.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS satisfies statutory/formal requirements for priority/benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of a priority or benefit claim in an ADS will satisfy the requirement in 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78 and the underlying statutory requirements (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 119, 120, 121, 365), and presentation of the name of the applicant in an ADS will satisfy 37 CFR 1.46 when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Law Treaty Model International Forms and the PCT Request Form can satisfy the ADS requirement for priority/benefit claims where indicated. However, a reference filing in an ADS under 37 CFR 1.57(a) that replaces the specification/drawings for purposes of a filing date is not by itself sufficient to establish a priority or benefit claim; applicants must still provide domestic or foreign priority/benefit information in the ADS as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office capture and non-review of ADS bibliographic information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will capture bibliographic information from the ADS and will generally not review the inventor's oath or declaration to determine consistency with the bibliographic information in the ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect bibliographic information in an ADS may be corrected as provided in the ADS correction/update procedures. Continuity data for the patent front page will be taken from the ADS; continuity data will not be included in the first sentence(s) of the specification unless applicant separately provides it there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application types and ADS applicability/limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An ADS may be submitted in provisional applications, nonprovisional applications, nonprovisional international design applications, and national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371. An ADS must be submitted when required by 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78 and when an application is filed by an assignee or person who shows sufficient proprietary interest (37 CFR 1.46).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain ADS capabilities (e.g., corrected Web-based ADS) are not permitted for international/national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, provisional, plant, reexamination, or supplemental examination proceedings. Some ADS-related CFR provisions differ for applications filed before September 16, 2012 (pre-AIA) and those filed on or after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative information in ADS does not constitute power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing practitioner registration numbers and representative information in the ADS does not itself constitute a power of attorney in the application (37 CFR 1.76(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office does not expect the ADS to be executed by the party who may appoint a power of attorney; a separate power of attorney document is required per 37 CFR 1.32.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant/assignee identification and assignment recording
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is filed by an assignee or other person under 37 CFR 1.46, the application must contain an ADS specifying the assignee or person in the applicant information section. Providing assignment information in the ADS does not substitute for compliance with requirements of 37 CFR part 3 to have an assignment recorded by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to correct or update the name of the applicant must include an ADS specifying the corrected name and comply with applicable correction provisions and part 3 recording requirements. Changes effective under Hague Agreement provisions will be recognized as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-suggested drawing figure for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may suggest a drawing figure for use on the front page of the patent application publication by including the suggestion on a compliant ADS timely filed before the publishing process begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may use the suggested figure but is not bound to do so; failure to use the suggested figure is not considered a material mistake for purposes of corrected publication under 37 CFR 1.221(b). See related USPTO guidance (Applicant-Suggested Drawing Figure in the Publication of Patent Applications).
